nodes.evidence: The ASan crash reads 252 bytes at nullable_memcpy; a read size of 252 (mdlen padded to 4) can only arise from decoding the untrusted 'md2=0x<hex>' payload into 'buf' at this scan (>= 249 bytes of hex). Reaching the sink therefore requires this source line to have executed. Crash stack frame #3 is parse_odp_push_nsh_action:2129, confirming the frame ran.

The memcpy READ size observed by ASan is exactly 252, which equals md_size (mdlen + 4-byte padding). The oversized md_size is thus witnessed at the sink as the memcpy length n=252 > sizeof(metadata)=248.

vul image crashes (stack-buffer-overflow READ 252) and fix image exits 0 with 'odp_actions_from_string: error' on the SAME PoC. The only functional change at this line is the added guard '&& n/2 <= sizeof metadata' (and sizing the stub with 'sizeof metadata'); the fix rejecting the input proves this missing bound is the root cause.

ASan: 'stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 252' at __asan_memcpy -> nullable_memcpy lib/util.h:173, over-reading 'metadata' (frame offset [160,408), 248 bytes) at offset 408 (4 bytes past end). Crash stack: nullable_memcpy <- nsh_key_to_attr <- parse_odp_push_nsh_action:2129.

edges.evidence: md_size=252 observed at sink is the padded decoded length of the md2 hex read into buf; the value chain buf->mdlen->md_size is required to produce the observed 252-byte read.
The memcpy length n equals md_size=252 (== ASan READ size), and src is the 248-byte 'metadata' stack array -> over-read. Confirmed by crash stack frames #1..#3.

edges.via: absent bound allows oversized md_size to reach the memcpy; adding the guard makes the parse return -EINVAL before the sink
edges.evidence: fix image (with the guard) exits 0 / rejects the action, never reaching the crash; vul image (without it) crashes at the sink.
